title: How Much Does Airbnb Take from Hosts in 2026?
summary: Airbnb takes 15.5% from most hosts in 2026 (16% in Brazil and Mexico), cleaning fee included. See the payout on a $550 booking and how Vrbo compares.
body_markdown:
Airbnb takes a[15.5% service fee](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/1857) from most hosts in 2026, deducted from your payout and charged on the nightly price plus any fees you add,[including the cleaning fee](https://www.airbnb.com/resources/hosting-homes/a/how-much-does-airbnb-charge-hosts-288) . Hosts with listings in Brazil and Mexico pay 16%. Under the single fee, guests no longer pay a separate Airbnb service fee on top of your price.


I checked every fee on this page against Airbnb's, Vrbo's and Booking.com's own pages on November 26, 2026.


## What percentage does Airbnb take from hosts?


Airbnb's single service fee is 15.5% for most hosts, typically 14% to 16% for the rest (Airbnb does not say who), and 16% for listings in Brazil and Mexico, according to[Airbnb's service fee article](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/1857) . The older split fee (3% from the host, 14.1% to 16.5% from the guest) still applies to hosts Airbnb has not migrated, and Airbnb is phasing it out. Airbnb describes the 15.5% rate as[its global average service fee](https://www.airbnb.com/resources/hosting-homes/a/simplifying-service-fees-on-airbnb-771) , and says the fee covers[payment processing, marketing and 24/7 support](https://www.airbnb.com/resources/hosting-homes/a/how-much-does-airbnb-charge-hosts-288) .


Fee structure Host pays Guest pays Who is on it Status (Nov 2026)


Single fee 15.5% for most hosts; typically 14% to 16% for the rest; 16% in Brazil and Mexico No separate service fee Most home hosts, hosts using property management software, hotels and serviced apartments Mandatory for most hosts ([Airbnb](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/1857) )


Split fee 3% for most hosts, more for some; 4% in Brazil and Mexico 14.1% to 16.5% of the booking subtotal Hosts Airbnb has not yet migrated Being phased out ([Airbnb](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/1857) )


## Who still pays the 3% split fee?


The 3% split fee still applies to home hosts Airbnb has not yet moved, and[Airbnb's service fee article](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/1857) says the structure "is being phased out and will no longer be available after all hosts are migrated." Airbnb does not say which accounts remain. On the split fee most hosts pay 3% and some pay more, listings in Brazil and Mexico pay 4%, and the guest pays 14.1% to 16.5% of the booking subtotal, and Airbnb adds an extra amount, still capped at 16.5%, when the guest pays in a different currency from your listing. Once your account moves to the single fee you can't switch back. Bookings made before the switch keep their old fee, even if the stay happens later. To see which structure a booking used, open the transaction in Earnings and look for the Airbnb service fee line.


## How did Airbnb's host fee change in 2025 and 2026?


Airbnb moved hosts to the 15.5% single fee in stages between August 2025 and October 2026, starting with hosts who connect through property management software (PMS). Airbnb has since rewritten its 2025 announcement, so the 2025 dates below come from the help centers of[Guesty](https://help.guesty.com/hc/en-gb/articles/9362649851037-Understanding-Airbnb-service-fees-for-hosts-and-guests) ,[Hostaway](https://support.hostaway.com/hc/en-us/articles/40440128540699-Airbnb-Fee-Structure-Changes-for-Hostaway-Users) and[OwnerRez](https://www.ownerrez.com/support/articles/mail-blast-2025-10-27-airbnb-new-single-fee-structure-now-live) . The 2026 dates come from Airbnb's Resource Center.


1. August 25, 2025: new host accounts that connected to a PMS or channel manager started on the 15.5% single fee.
2. October 27, 2025: PMS-connected hosts on the split fee were moved to the single fee, and hosts already on the older 15% single fee went up half a point.
3. December 1, 2025: hosts without a PMS who had opted into the 15% single fee also went to 15.5%.
4. May 25 and June 22, 2026: hosts living in Peru and South Korea switched in May, Germany and the UK in June ([Airbnb](https://www.airbnb.com/resources/hosting-homes/a/simplifying-service-fees-761) ).
5. September 15 and October 13, 2026: Airbnb's deadlines for the remaining hosts to adjust their prices, September 15 outside the European Economic Area and October 13 inside it or in Switzerland ([Airbnb](https://www.airbnb.com/resources/hosting-homes/a/simplifying-service-fees-on-airbnb-771) ).
6. October 13, 2026: PMS users "who weren't yet on the single service fee" switched, so the October 2025 move had not covered every PMS-connected account ([Airbnb](https://www.airbnb.com/resources/hosting-homes/a/simplifying-airbnb-service-fees-746) ).


## How much does Airbnb take from a $150-a-night booking?


On a 3-night stay at $150 a night with a $100 cleaning fee, the subtotal is $550 and Airbnb's 15.5% single fee takes $85.25, leaving a $464.75 payout. The guest pays $550 plus taxes. In Brazil or Mexico, at 16%, the fee is $88.00 and the payout $462.00.


Under the old split fee, the same $550 booking cost the host 3%, or $16.50, for a $533.50 payout. The guest paid a further 14.1% to 16.5% ($77.55 to $90.75), so the checkout total was $627.55 to $640.75 before taxes.


To keep the $533.50 payout under the single fee, divide it by 0.845 (what is left after 15.5%). The subtotal has to be $631.36, about 14.8% above $550. That price sits inside the $627.55 to $640.75 range the guest used to pay at checkout, so a host who reprices correctly keeps both the payout and the guest's total close to where they were.


## How do you raise prices so your payout stays the same?


Raising prices by about 15% keeps your payout the same. In[Airbnb's own example](https://www.airbnb.com/resources/hosting-homes/a/simplifying-service-fees-on-airbnb-771) , guests saw $115 on a $100 listing and Airbnb paid the host $97. Under the single fee you set the price at $115, the guest still sees $115, and you earn about $97 ($115 less 15.5% is $97.18). Leave the price at $100 and you earn $84.50. Raise your cleaning, pet and other fees by the same proportion as the nightly rate, because Airbnb charges the 15.5% on all of them.


Hosts who don't use a PMS can apply Airbnb's[price adjustment tool](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/4095) , which changes nightly prices and host fees (but not discounts) for the next two years of your calendar in one step. Hosts on a PMS set the increase as an Airbnb channel markup in their software.


## What else comes out of an Airbnb payout?


VAT on Airbnb's service fee and payout method fees can reduce what reaches your bank account after the 15.5% fee, and so can occupancy tax if you build it into your nightly price. Airbnb's own VAT example charges the VAT on top of its service fee, so in a 20% VAT country the $550 example loses another $17.05 (20% of $85.25), for a payout of $447.70.


Airbnb adds VAT to the host service fee in countries that tax electronically supplied services, and in some of them it does not charge VAT to a host who has registered a VAT ID ([Airbnb VAT article](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/436) ). For a host in a 20% VAT country who is not VAT registered,[Airbnb's price adjustment tool](https://www.airbnb.com/resources/hosting-homes/a/simplifying-service-fees-on-airbnb-771) raises a $100 listing to $119 instead of $115 to cover that VAT. A VAT-registered host who self-assesses keeps the $115 price and accounts for the VAT separately.


Airbnb collects and remits occupancy taxes from guests in the[jurisdictions it lists](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/2509) , and those taxes sit on top of your price. Everywhere else you collect them yourself, either through Airbnb's custom tax tool or by building the tax into your nightly price ([Airbnb policy](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/2799) ). Built into the price, the tax comes out of your payout and Airbnb's fee applies to it too.


Airbnb usually releases a payout[within 1 business day after check-in](https://www.airbnb.com/resources/hosting-homes/a/how-youll-get-paid-for-hosting-20) . US hosts using[Fast Pay](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/3326) get the money within 30 minutes and pay 1.5% per payout, capped at $15, which is $6.97 on the $464.75 payout above. US direct deposit (ACH) has no fee, while Airbnb says fees may apply to PayPal and international wire and do apply to Western Union ([payout methods](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/54) ). On[international transfers](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/321) , your bank and any intermediary bank can charge their own fees, which Airbnb does not control.


## How much does Airbnb take from Experiences and Services hosts?


Airbnb typically charges Experiences hosts 20% and Services hosts 15%, with a $6 minimum fee on each Services booking, per the[Experiences and Services section of its fee page](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/1857) . Airbnb takes $20 from a $100 Experience. On a $30 Service, 15% would be $4.50, so the $6 minimum applies and the host keeps $24.


## Does Airbnb charge more for strict cancellation policies?


Airbnb's[service fee article](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/1857) lists no extra host fee tied to a cancellation policy; its rates vary only by fee structure, by host, and for listings in Brazil and Mexico. Strict, Super Strict 30 Days and Super Strict 60 Days are available[only by invitation from Airbnb](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/475) . The standard policies open to every host are Flexible, Moderate, Limited and Firm.


## How do Airbnb fees compare with Vrbo and Booking.com?


Against Airbnb's 15.5%, Vrbo charges a 12% commission and Booking.com sets yours in the agreement you sign at registration. Vrbo's new rate started on October 29, 2026 ([Expedia Group newsroom](https://www.expedia.com/newsroom/vrbo-compensation-model-changes/) ). It covers the[rent plus host fees](https://help.vrbo.com/articles/How-is-the-booking-fee-calculated) and includes payment processing when Vrbo collects the payment, and the annual subscription plan is being retired. Hosts using their own payment processor pay 12% plus that processor's fees, and some Professional Plan hosts in Europe, Australia and New Zealand pay up to 15%. On the $550 example, Vrbo's 12% is $66.00 and the payout is $484.00 before any VAT. Vrbo also charges travelers a service fee on top of that $550 and does not publish its range, so a Vrbo guest pays more than $550 while the Airbnb guest pays $550.


Booking.com shows the commission percentage at the "Agreement" step of sign-up and invoices it monthly, with no commission on free cancellations ([Booking.com FAQ](https://join.booking.com/faq.html) ). If you use[Payments by Booking.com](https://partner.booking.com/en-us/help/policies-payments/payment-products/how-much-payments-bookingcom-costs) with bank-transfer payouts, a payment fee applies that depends on your property's location, and[Booking.com's sign-up page](https://join.booking.com/faq.html) advertises that fee as waived for 2026. For the cost math across OTA commissions, see[OTA commission vs AI agent bookings](https://www.conduit.ai/blog/ota-commission-vs-ai-agent-bookings) , and for the channel with no OTA commission (you still pay card processing),[how to get more direct bookings](https://www.conduit.ai/blog/how-to-get-more-direct-bookings-for-your-vacation-rentals-in-2024) .


If you list on more than one of these sites, Conduit answers guest messages from Airbnb, Vrbo, Booking.com and direct bookings in one inbox, in 140+ languages. See how it handles[Airbnb guest messaging](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/short-term-rentals/airbnb-messaging) .


## FAQ


A payout lower than you expected usually comes from one of a few places: the booking was made after your account switched to the single fee, your cleaning and pet fees were not raised along with the nightly price, or VAT was added to Airbnb's service fee. Check the booking's Earnings breakdown before contacting support.


### Is Airbnb's host fee 3% or 15.5%?


Most hosts now pay 15.5%, because Airbnb has moved them to the single service fee (16% in Brazil and Mexico). The 3% rate survives only for hosts still on the split fee, whose guests pay 14.1% to 16.5% on top.


### Does Airbnb take its fee from the cleaning fee?


Yes. The 15.5% applies to the cleaning fee, pet fee and any other fee you add, as well as the nightly price, but not to taxes.


### Can I switch back to the 3% split fee?


No. Airbnb does not let a host return to the split fee after moving to the single fee, although reservations made before the move keep their original fee.


### How much should I raise my Airbnb prices to keep the same payout?


About 15%, applied to the nightly price and every host fee. A booking that paid $533.50 under the 3% split fee needs a $631.36 subtotal under the 15.5% single fee.


### What does Airbnb charge for Fast Pay?


Fast Pay is a US-only option that costs 1.5% of each payout, up to $15. Regular US direct deposit is free.


### Is Vrbo cheaper than Airbnb for hosts?


Vrbo's standard host commission is 12% (up to 15% on some regional plans) against Airbnb's 15.5%, so on a $550 booking Vrbo takes $66.00 and Airbnb takes $85.25. Vrbo also adds a traveler service fee at checkout, so its guest pays more than $550.


### Does Airbnb charge hosts VAT?


In countries that tax electronically supplied services, yes, on top of the service fee. In some of them a VAT-registered host who adds a VAT ID and self-assesses is not charged.
